title: Money & currency
body:
Andorra's currency is the euro, even though it isn't an EU member — a bilateral monetary agreement lets it mint its own coins. Cards, contactless, Apple Pay and Google Pay are accepted almost everywhere; carry some cash for small old-town cafés and market stalls.

Andorra runs its own sales tax, the IGI, at a flat {{fact:igi-tax-4-5-percent}} general rate — well below Spain's 21% or France's 20% VAT, which is why electronics, cosmetics, spirits and eyewear are noticeably cheaper here. There is no special tax-free counter: the low rate applies in every shop, to residents and visitors alike.

title: Budget & daily costs
intro: Rough per-person, per-day USD estimates for a Nov (low-season) trip — treat every figure as ≈ and confirm at booking; flight and lodging prices shift with dates and demand.

items.note: ≈ — a borda dinner runs €35–50pp; old-town lunches and pastries are cheaper

items.label: Local transport, per day
items.note: Andorra la Vella's old quarter and most sights are walkable; occasional local bus or taxi
